properties.name: Every served tool carries a short title, and every writing tool says whether it can destroy (destructiveHint), so a chat directory that requires both lists reflow2's tools as they are
properties.statement:
Every tool reflow2 serves carries MCP's `title` annotation (a short human name, distinct from its id) and, on every writing tool, `destructiveHint` (true where a call can delete or overwrite what a person made: delete_node, delete_edge, apply_heal, export_graph with overwrite, …; false where it only adds or revises with the prior state preserved). `readOnlyHint` is already on all of them.
WHY: flo2 serves reflow2's tools unchanged through its chat door, and Anthony means to list that door in the Claude Connectors Directory, whose production standards ask for a clear title and read/write hints on every tool (flo2's req:flo2s-chat-door-is-listed-in-the-claude-connectors-directory-once-its-tools-are-annotated-and-the-gate-is-settled, and integrated-flo's umbrella requirement, both 2026-10-10). Levied on reflow2 by flo2's design: of what the directory asks, only these two annotations are reflow2's to supply.
MEASURED 2026-10-10 on main (e40481148, reports 0.81.1), `--list-tools --full` over 197 tools: title 0 of 197; readOnlyHint 197 of 197; destructiveHint 7 of 197 (119 are write tools); idempotentHint 1; openWorldHint 0.
HOW, left to the build: the title lives beside the description in each tool's `#[tool]` attribute, so the toolsnap goldens (ver:the-served-tool-surface-matches-its-goldens) change once and then hold it; a test counts titles and destructive hints over tools/list so a new tool cannot arrive without them. This is additive: no argument or reply changes, so MCP consumers such as Alex see only new annotation fields.
